 MACA NO. 741 OF 2016  2  2025:KER:1025 N.R.Thomas vs The National Insurance Co.Ltd on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170726094/

sentences.text: The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.)No.1121/2013 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam is the appellant herein.

The 3rd respondent in the O.P.
is the respondent herein.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident that occurred on 27.03.2013.

2. According to the petitioner, on 27.03.2013 at about 09.30 p.m, while he was walking along Arakuzha - Muvattupuzha road,, a car bearing Registration No.KL-02/X 7648 driven by the 2nd respondent hit him down.
As a result of which, he sustained serious injuries.
The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to him, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.6,87,000/-.
3. The 1st and 2nd respondents entered appearance, but did not file any written statement.
The 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence MACA NO. 741 OF 2016 2025:KER:1025 of the petitioner.
4. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A20 and Ext.C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,05,580/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
8. Heard Sri.K.Janardhanan, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri.P.K.Manoj Kumar, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
9. The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
Though in the written statement the 3rd respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner, at the time of arguments such a contention was not taken.
The petitioner has produced Ext.A3, copy of the charge sheet involved in the crime registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, in respect to the above accident.
In the MACA NO. 741 OF 2016 2025:KER:1025 light of the above charge sheet, negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stands proved.

Therefore, the 3rd respondent, being the insurer, is liable to indemnify the N.R.Thomas vs The National Insurance Co.Ltd on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170726094/
2 compensation, which is liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 10. The petitioner was aged 52 years on the date of the accident, on 27.03.2013.
According to the petitioner, he was a carpenter by profession, earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Since he could not prove the income claimed in the OP, the Tribunal fixed his income at Rs.7,000/-.

In the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manger,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie is liable to be fixed at Rs.9,000/- during 2013.

sentences.text: Considsering the fact that, the petitioner is a carpenter by profession, his notional income during the year 2013 is fixed at Rs.10,000/-.

11. In the accident the petitioner sustained comminuted fracture to posterior wall of left acetabulam,
injuries to maxillary with central dislocation of femoral head.
He was treated as inpatient from 28.03.2013 to 11.05. 2013.
Open reduction and internal fixation were done.
Luxated teeth and injuries to eyes were also noticed.
Ext.C1 -disability certificate issued by the medical board, showing that he has a permanent disability of 17%.
However, in the said certificate, it is MACA NO. 741 OF 2016 2025:KER:1025 specifically noted that it is not possible for the petitioner to work in cross legged position.
Ext.C1 further states that implant in SITU is not removable.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that though the permanent physical disability of the petitioner aa shown in Ext.C1 was only 17%, his functional disability is much higher, as he could not proceed with his job as a carpenter.
The petitioner appeared before the Court and on examination, it was revealed that he could not even sit.
In the above circumstances, I am satisfied that the functional disability of the petitioner is much more than 17% shown in Ext.C1.Considering
the fact that he is a carpenter by profession and he could not sit to work in a cross-legged position

, his functional disability is fixed at 40%.
12.

Since, on the date of accident, he was aged 52 years, 10 % of his income is to be added towards future prospects, and the multiplier to be applied is 11, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. In the above circumstances, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.5,80,000/-.
14. Towards the head 'loss of earnings', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/-, when his monthly income was treated as Rs.7,000/-.

Since his notional income was refixed to Rs.10,000/-,
compensation under the head 'loss of MACA NO. 741 OF 2016 2025:KER:1025 earnings'
correspondingly enhanced to Rs.85,000/-.
Another Rs.20,000/- awarded on the head 'Compensation for loss of earning power' is, therefore deducted.
15. Towards the head 'extra nourishment', the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.3,000/-.

Considering the fact that the petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the incident and his functional disability is estimated at 40%, I hold that the compensation awarded on the head extra nourishment is on the lesser side and hence it is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the petitioner, is on the lower side.

sentences.text: He sustained fracture left acetabulam with central dislocation of femoral head.
Open reduction and internal fixation were done.
In the medical records, it is seen that he has sustained comminuted fracture to posterior wall of acetabulam and injuries to his maxillary.
It is also revealed that, he is not in a position to work in cross-legged position.
This Court has already found that, his functional disability will come to 40%.

Therefore,
the compensation awarded on the head pain and suffering is also lower side and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.1,50,000/-.
17. Towards the head compensation for loss of amenities, the Tribunal MACA NO. 741 OF 2016 2025:KER:1025 has not awarded any compensation.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, I hold that a sum of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded on the said head.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.10,50,500/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.
